# groups declared and tightened in named instances — `features/`

## Project layout

    features/
    ├─ checkout/ ❗                    (instance of [feature]/)
    │
    ├─ orders/ ❗                      (instance of [feature]/)
    │
    └─ [feature]/ 0+
       └─ steps/
          │
          └─ [num=0000]_[t=a+].sql 0+  a migration step

❗ marks a named file or directory that must exist; one without it may be absent. A count after a pattern, such as `0+` or `1+`, is the fewest matching names that must exist.

In `[num=0000]`, the text after `=` is a mask: each character matches one character of the name. `0` matches a digit and `a` a lowercase letter. `+` repeats the element before it one or more times. `espalier help matching` has the full grammar.

## `[feature]/`

Concrete instances:
- `checkout/`, in `checkout/AGENTS.MD`
- `orders/`, in `orders/AGENTS.MD`

### Adding new instances

A `[feature]/` directory needs no declaration. Declaring one gives it its own guidance; see `espalier help instances`.

## `[feature]/steps/[num=0000]_[t=a+].sql` — a migration step

### Together, by `num` — one release

A step migrates one thing.

Declared groups, each bound by this grouping and by its own section:

#### `[feature]/steps/0009_[t=a+].sql` — the reserved step

Step 0009 is reserved for data fixes, in every feature.

#### Adding new groups

A `step` group needs no declaration. Declaring one gives it its own guidance; see `espalier help instances`.
